source: UN News Cholera Southern Africa Zimbabwe February 2009
processing_notes: Source states: 'Botswana, which is not endemic for cholera, has eight cases' - interpreted as 8 sCh cases by Feb 13 2009. Cases linked to spread from Zimbabwe 2008-2009 outbreak. Palm Tree village (near Zimbabwe border) confirmed. This early count preceded the full outbreak total documented in source 2.

Source states: 'Botswana recorded 55 suspected cases of cholera, with 15 confirmed cases resulting in two deaths' as of March 18 2009. Vibrio cholerae detected in Shashe reservoir near Tonota and Letsibogo Dam. Cases linked to Zimbabwe 2008-2009 cross-border outbreak. CFR = 2/55 = 3.6%. Note: JHU baseline has annual 2009 data showing 15 cases 2 deaths - these are the same outbreak reported at different points in time. This source provides the fuller suspected/confirmed breakdown at outbreak peak.

source: WHO AFRO Botswana Diarrhoea Outbreak Response 2018
processing_notes: Source states: 'Between 8th and 19th October 2018, the NHL cultured 22 stool specimens and all the specimens were negative for Vibrio cholerae.' Additionally: 'No suspected cholera cases have been detected in Botswana in recent times.' - confirms zero cholera transmission during diarrhoea outbreak investigation period. Surveillance system was operational: 22 specimens tested. Rotavirus identified as cause. Evidence type: Documented_Absence from WHO AFRO laboratory investigation report.

source: Xinhua Botswana First Suspected Cholera Case June 2023
processing_notes: Source states first-ever suspected cholera case reported June 15 2023 in Somerset suburb of Francistown; health minister stated 'It is suspected that a probable case of cholera has been detected.' Per follow-up confirmation, National Health Laboratory confirmatory tests came out negative for cholera despite initial positive rapid diagnostic test. Zero confirmed cholera cases. Surveillance system operational with laboratory confirmation capacity. Evidence type: Documented_Absence confirmed by National Health Laboratory negative result.

source: Botswana Daily News Cholera Prevention Commitment 2024
processing_notes: Source states: 'Botswana has so far not recorded any cholera case' (February 2024). Botswana not listed among 14 WHO AFRO affected countries in 2024 (Burundi, Cameroon, Comoros, DRC, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Government confirmed commitment to preventive measures while neighboring Zimbabwe and Zambia experienced outbreaks. Evidence type: Documented_Absence from government news report and WHO AFRO regional data.

source: WHO AFRO Monthly Regional Cholera Bulletin 2025
processing_notes: Source states the WHO African Region cholera outbreak in 2025 affected the following 20 countries: 'Angola, Burundi, Comoros, Cote d'Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, South Sudan, Togo, the United Republic of Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe' - interpreted as 0 cholera cases for Botswana, which is absent from this comprehensive list of active African Region countries despite outbreaks in bordering Namibia, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Cross-confirmed by ECDC December 2025 overview (top African burden countries listed without Botswana) and WHO multi-country sitreps #28 and epi update #33 which do not mention Botswana. Evidence type: Documented_Absence via clear absence from comprehensive multi-country WHO AFRO reporting table listing all active countries.

source: WHO Multi-country Cholera Epidemiological Update 33 January 2026
processing_notes: Source (WHO multi-country cholera epidemiological update #33, 27 January 2026; reporting period 1 January to 28 December 2025 plus January 2026) states cases reported from listed WHO regions; Botswana is not mentioned anywhere in this document. January 2026 new cases reported from 19 countries across three WHO regions, Botswana not among them. No cholera cases reported in Botswana for the partial 2026 period to date. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence for partial-year 2026 - Botswana absent from WHO multi-country reporting but year incomplete; lower confidence pending full-year confirmation.
